The US government announced yesterday an update to its list of prohibited foreign-made products, adding "advanced robotic devices" to the roster. A Federal Communications Commission (FCC) spokesperson confirmed today that the ban also applies to robot vacuums.

The robot vacuum ban affects Roomba, Roborock, and other major brands—but your existing robot vacuum can continue to be used

When the Trump administration announced yesterday a ban on "advanced robotic devices" entering the US, headlines focused on humanoid robots. But espionage doesn't require legs—and the FCC's robot ban won't discriminate either. Katie Gorscak, the FCC's director of media relations, confirmed to The Verge that robot vacuums will fall under the scope of the ban. Authorities won't be coming to seize your existing Roomba—businesses can continue importing and selling already-approved products. However, the government claims future foreign-made robots will pose national security risks, and even robot vacuum companies have suddenly been required to commit to manufacturing within the United States.

The FCC's logic that advanced robotic devices pose national security risks applies equally to products generally considered harmless—robot vacuums, robotic lawn mowers, and so forth.

Unless a device is explicitly approved, or manufactured domestically in the US, it will not be allowed to be sold locally.

This ban has particularly far-reaching implications for the robot vacuum market, as top brands such as Roomba, Roborock, and Ecovacs are all owned by Chinese companies.

If you currently own any of the aforementioned products, you can continue using them today without any impact. The FCC won't send anyone to confiscate your robot vacuum.

However, depending on how the ban is enforced, the robot vacuum market could see dramatic upheaval in the short term. If all this sounds familiar, it's because the ban is virtually identical to the one targeting wireless routers just a few months ago.

Will you continue using your existing robot vacuum? Why? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
